tasks.title: Lecture #47
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a biology class.
tasks.transcript:
Man: The phenomenon of animal migration is a fascinating subject in biology. Migration involves the regular, often seasonal movement of animals from one region to another, typically in search of food, breeding grounds, or better climates. This behavior is observed in a wide variety of species, including birds, mammals, fish, and insects.
One of the most well known examples is the migration of monarch butterflies. These butterflies travel thousands of miles from North America to central Mexico to escape the cold winter. This journey involves multiple generations, as no single butterfly makes the round trip.
Another remarkable example is the migration of humpback whales. These massive creatures travel from their feeding grounds in polar waters to warmer tropical regions where they breed and give birth.
Birds like the Arctic tern undertake one of the longest migrations, traveling from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back each year. Despite their differences in size, species and reasons for migrating, they all migrate vast distances with precision. They navigate like seasoned human pilots flying transcontinental routes, only without aircraft, instruments or GPS.
Of course, migration is not without its challenges. Animals must navigate vast distances, often facing predators, adverse weather and human made obstacles like buildings and roads. Protecting habitats and reducing human interference can help maintain the delicate balance that allows migration to occur. Understanding animal migration provides insight into the complex behaviors and survival strategies of various species.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: The feeding habits of migratory animals
options.D: Navigational methods used by migrating animals

questions.analysis: 答案： B 题目问的是: 这篇讲座的主要话题是什么？ 定位原文: "The phenomenon of animal migration is a fascinating subject in biology...Migration involves the regular... movement... in search of food, breeding grounds... One of the most well known examples... Another remarkable example..." 选项分析: A. The feeding habits of migratory animals (迁徙动物的进食习惯) - 错误。虽然提到了寻找食物，但这只是迁徙的原因之一，不是全文主旨。 B. Animal migration and its characteristics (动物迁徙及其特征) - 正确。讲座首先定义了迁徙，然后列举了帝王蝶、座头鲸、北极燕鸥等例子来说明迁徙的距离、代际特征和导航能力，最后讨论了面临的挑战，全面涵盖了迁徙的特征。 C. Challenges faced by migratory species (迁徙物种面临的挑战) - 错误。这只是讲座最后一部分的内容，不能概括全文。 D. Navigational methods used by migrating animals (迁徙动物使用的导航方法) - 错误。讲座提到了导航的精准性，但并未详细展开具体的“方法”（如磁场、星象等），只是将其作为一个特征来描述。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention human pilots?

options.A: To illustrate the complexity of animal navigation
options.B: To suggest that birds might follow flight paths
options.C: To discuss the impact of airplanes on the climate
options.D: To describe human interference in migration

questions.analysis: 答案: A 题目问的是: 说话者为什么提到人类飞行员？ 定位原文: "They navigate like seasoned human pilots flying transcontinental routes, only without aircraft, instruments or GPS." 选项分析: A. To illustrate the complexity of animal navigation (为了说明动物导航的复杂性/高超性) -正确。说话者通过将动物比作“经验丰富的飞行员”，强调了动物在没有高科技辅助的情况下，能像人类一样精准地进行长距离导航，突出了其导航能力的高超和复杂。 B. To suggest that birds might follow flight paths (为了暗示鸟类可能遵循飞行路径) - 错误。重点在于导航能力的对比，而非具体的路线。 C. To discuss the impact of airplanes on the climate (为了讨论飞机对气候的影响) - 错误。与讲座内容无关。 D. To describe human interference in migration (为了描述人类对迁徙的干扰) - 错误。虽然讲座后文提到了人类干扰，但提到飞行员是为了做导航能力的类比，而非指干扰。

questions.stem: What is unusual about the migration of monarch butterflies?

options.A: They migrate from a colder to a warmer region.
options.B: Their migration requires precise navigation skills.
options.C: A single migration occurs over multiple generations.
options.D: A migrating monarch eats nothing until it reaches its destination.

questions.analysis: 答案: C 题目问的是: 帝王蝶的迁徙有什么不寻常之处？ 定位原文: "This journey involves multiple generations, as no single butterfly makes the round trip." 选项分析: A. They migrate from a colder to a warmer region. (它们从较冷地区迁徙到较暖地区。) -错误。这是许多迁徙动物的共同特征（如座头鲸），不是帝王蝶独有的不寻常之处。 B. Their migration requires precise navigation skills. (它们的迁徙需要精准的导航技能。) -错误。这也是许多迁徙动物的共同特征。 C. A single migration occurs over multiple generations. (单次迁徙过程跨越了多代。) - 正确。文中明确指出“no single butterfly makes the round trip”，即往返旅程需要多代蝴蝶接力完成，这是其独特之处。 D. A migrating monarch eats nothing until it reaches its destination. (迁徙的帝王蝶在到达目的地前不吃任何东西。) - 错误。文中未提及。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention"human-made obstacles"?

options.A: To explain how animals adapt to urban environments
options.B: To contrast migration by sea to migration over land
options.C: To describe a common reason for animal migration
options.D: To emphasize the need to protect migratory routes

questions.analysis: 答案: D 题目问的是: 说话者为什么提到“人为障碍”？ 定位原文: "Animals must navigate vast distances, often facing predators, adverse weather and human made obstacles like buildings and roads. Protecting habitats and reducing human interference can help maintain the delicate balance..." 选项分析: A. To explain how animals adapt to urban environments (为了解释动物如何适应城市环境)- 错误。文中强调的是这些障碍是挑战，而非适应。 B. To contrast migration by sea to migration over land (为了对比海上迁徙和陆地迁徙) -错误。文中未进行此类对比。 C. To describe a common reason for animal migration (为了描述动物迁徙的一个常见原因)- 错误。人为障碍是迁徙途中遇到的困难，不是迁徙的原因。 D. To emphasize the need to protect migratory routes (为了强调保护迁徙路线的必要性) -正确。提到人为障碍（如建筑物和道路）是为了引出后文的结论：我们需要“保护栖息地”和“减少人为干扰”，即保护迁徙路线。
